annotation_description: Playing Island instead of Forest means they cannot cast Wild Growth on turn 2 (which requires G and enchants a land to ramp). With Forest, they could play Wild Growth turn 2 on the Forest, then have access to GG on turn 3 plus whatever other land they play. Alternatively, Forest enables casting Serum Visions only if they draw a U source, but Island enables Serum Visions turn 2 to dig. However, Terramorphic Expanse is also in hand and can fetch either basic. The optimal line is likely Forest now, then Terramorphic Expanse turn 2 (crack for Island), enabling Wild Growth on Forest turn 2 for strong ramp. Playing Island first delays the Wild Growth plan by a turn. That said, Island enables turn 2 Serum Visions which has value for finding lands, so this is debatable but Forest is generally better here for the ramp plan.

message: Select cards to PUT on the BOTTOM of your library (Scry) (selected 0 of 2)
annotation_description: Winged Boots is a cheap Equipment with excellent synergy with Galea (can be cast from top of library, provides flying and ward {4} protection). Ride the Avalanche is more situational and requires specific timing to be effective. Bottoming Winged Boots over Ride the Avalanche loses a consistently strong Galea synergy piece.

Playing Dimir Aqueduct as the only land on turn 1 means it enters tapped AND requires bouncing a land you control. Since Haiku Villain has no other lands in play, they must bounce the Aqueduct itself back to hand, completely wasting the turn with no land on the battlefield. This sets them back an entire turn compared to playing Island or Halimar Depths.

Discarding Island when they have zero lands on the battlefield and only 3 lands in hand. Dimir Aqueduct can't be played until another land is in play (needs to bounce a land), so discarding Island leaves them with only Halimar Depths as a playable land on turn 2, making them very dependent on drawing lands.

Cast Chittering Witch before playing a land drop. They had Mountain and Swamp in hand and could have played one first to have 5 mana available instead of 4, which would be relevant for Chittering Witch's activated ability ({1}{B}, Sacrifice a creature) if needed during opponents' turns.

Fetching Forest when Plains would provide better color balance. With Plains from fetch + Forest from hand on turn 2, Timmy would have access to G, W, and U immediately, enabling earlier Fleecemane Lion and Angelic Gift. With Forest, white mana is delayed until Sungrass Prairie (which costs 1 to activate, effectively delaying GW access).

Playing Halimar Depths before Dimir Aqueduct is poor land sequencing. With no lands on the battlefield, this is the perfect time to play Dimir Aqueduct (enters tapped with no land to bounce back). Next turn, Haiku Villain will likely play Dimir Aqueduct and be forced to bounce Halimar Depths back to hand, losing a turn of land development. Playing Aqueduct now means turn 3 could have Swamp untapped + Aqueduct for 3 mana (UBB), enabling Loyal Subordinate or Dimir Signet.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the TOP of your library (last one chosen will be topmost)
annotation_description: Put Adarkar Valkyrie on top of library instead of Arcane Sanctum. On turn 2 with early mana development needs (Dimir Signet, Mind Stone in hand), drawing a land next is more useful than drawing a 6-mana creature that won't be castable for several turns.

Playing Mountain instead of Swamp leaves Sonnet Stoic unable to cast Danse Macabre ({3}{B}{B}) next turn. With Swamp, they'd have access to both Karazikar ({3}{B}{R}) and Danse Macabre on turn 4. With Mountain, only Karazikar is castable.

Cast Karazikar before playing a land from hand. Sonnet Stoic has a Swamp and Mountain in hand and only 3 lands on the battlefield. Playing a land first is free and would leave them with 4 lands after casting Karazikar instead of 3 (with a land drop still available but all mana tapped).

Casting Wild Growth before playing a land is a sequencing error. The player has Sungrass Prairie, Forest, and Lumbering Falls in hand but only 2 lands on the battlefield. They should play a land first to ensure they don't miss a land drop, then cast Wild Growth. More importantly, playing Sungrass Prairie first (which enters untapped) or Forest would give them more options. With Forest + Island + Wild Growth on the Forest, they'd have access to GGU next turn. But if they play the land first, they can still cast Wild Growth with the Forest they already have. The main issue is casting a spell before making the land drop - if they play Lumbering Falls (enters tapped) or Sungrass Prairie, they still have G available from Forest to cast Wild Growth. Playing the land first is strictly better sequencing since it preserves information and ensures the land drop isn't forgotten.

Gem25F Timmy's hand contains Fleecemane Lion (GW), Sungrass Prairie (needs 1+T for GW), Lumbering Falls (enters tapped, produces G or U), and Forest. The commander Galea costs 1GWU. Putting Wild Growth on Island gives the Island the ability to produce U+G when tapped. However, Timmy's color needs are primarily G and W - they already have an Island for U. Putting Wild Growth on Forest would give Forest the ability to produce G+G, which combined with the Island (U) and a Sungrass Prairie (GW) would provide better mana flexibility. More importantly, with Fleecemane Lion costing GW as the most likely next play, and Sungrass Prairie requiring 1+T to produce GW, putting Wild Growth on Forest means tapping Forest produces GG, enabling turn 3 Fleecemane Lion with Forest(GG via Wild Growth) + Island(U) + Sungrass Prairie(1,T->GW) - wait, that doesn't work either since Sungrass Prairie needs 1 generic. Actually, looking more carefully: with Wild Growth on Island, tapping Island gives U+G (2 mana), then Forest gives G, and if they play Sungrass Prairie (enters untapped), they'd need to pay 1+T for GW from it. For Fleecemane Lion (GW): Forest(G) + Sungrass Prairie requires 1 generic mana to activate. With Wild Growth on Forest: Forest gives G+G, Island gives U, Sungrass Prairie needs 1+T. Either way they can cast Fleecemane Lion next turn (Forest for G, pay 1 into Sungrass Prairie using the extra mana from Wild Growth). Actually Wild Growth on Forest is likely slightly better since it accelerates green mana which is more needed for the GW-heavy cards in hand (Fleecemane Lion, Ride the Avalanche has G). The difference is small but putting it on Forest is marginally better for the mana base.

Ride the Avalanche is an instant that gives your next spell flash and puts +1/+1 counters on a creature when you cast that next spell. Cast during precombat main with no creatures on the battlefield and before playing a land, this wastes the card almost entirely. The player has Fleecemane Lion in hand but only 2 mana sources available after casting Ride the Avalanche (Forest tapped for G, Island tapped for U via Wild Growth). They can't cast any follow-up spell this turn. Ride the Avalanche's effect only lasts until end of turn, so the flash-granting and counter-placing abilities are completely wasted. The card is thrown away for zero value.

Played Forest instead of Sungrass Prairie when holding Fleecemane Lion (GW) and Angelic Gift (1W) with no white mana sources. Sungrass Prairie would enable casting white spells on future turns, while a basic Forest provides redundant green mana.

Playing Dimir Aqueduct with only one land on battlefield (Halimar Depths) means bouncing that land, resulting in zero mana available this turn and effectively losing a full turn of development. With Karazikar already on the opposing board threatening damage, falling further behind on tempo is very costly.

Discarded Pilgrim's Eye, which is a cheap creature that searches for a basic land - exactly what this mana-screwed player needs (only 1 land on battlefield). Adarkar Valkyrie costs 4WW and the player has zero white mana sources on board or in hand, making it extremely difficult to cast anytime soon.

Failed to play the Swamp from hand before casting Prosper, Tome-Bound. Playing the land first would leave an additional B mana available after casting Prosper, which could enable Chittering Witch's activated ability ({1}{B}, sacrifice a creature) for defensive purposes.

Player had enough mana to cast both Fleecemane Lion (GW) and Sword of Hours (2) this turn, but only cast Fleecemane Lion. With Sol Ring (CC), Forest+Wild Growth (GG), Island (U), and Sungrass Prairie (1+T: GW), there was plenty of mana to deploy both. Additionally, they should play Lumbering Falls (the Unknown choice) as their land drop before casting spells.

Should have played the Swamp from hand before casting the creature to have 6 mana available. Additionally, Yavimaya Elder is likely the stronger play here - in a multiplayer game on turn 4, the land ramp and card draw from Elder provides more long-term value than a 3/2 hexproof body. Elder dying to Karazikar-forced attacks would actually be beneficial, fetching 2 lands.

Sonnet Stoic cast Danse Macabre without first playing a land from hand. They had Swamp and Mountain available to play. Playing Swamp first would have provided the second black mana needed, saving the Treasure token that was sacrificed to help pay for the spell. The Treasure token represents future mana flexibility that was needlessly spent.

Casting Fleecemane Lion before combat is suboptimal when holding Angelic Gift (which could be used as a combat trick to grant flying and draw a card) and Valorous Stance (indestructible or removal). By casting the creature pre-combat, Timmy reveals information unnecessarily and loses the option to hold up mana for tricks. Additionally, Lumbering Falls could have been activated as a 3/3 attacker this turn, and casting the Lion pre-combat means less mana available for other plays. More importantly, if Timmy wanted to equip Sword of Hours to a creature and attack, playing the Lion post-combat would have been equivalent since it has summoning sickness anyway - but the mana spent now can't be used for Valorous Stance if needed during combat.

Casting Valorous Stance during precombat main phase without an immediate threat to respond to. Valorous Stance is an instant-speed combat trick or removal spell that is almost always better held up as a reactive play. Using it proactively here means either destroying a creature preemptively (when it could be saved for a more critical threat) or granting indestructible to nothing meaningful. Additionally, casting spells before combat when holding Angelic Gift (which could be a combat trick giving flying + drawing a card) and with Sword of Hours on board suggests poor sequencing - Fleecemane Lion should likely be cast first, then equipment attached, then consider combat before using removal/protection spells.

annotation_description: There are no creatures with toughness 4 or greater on the battlefield. Troll Ascetic is 3/2 (and has hexproof), Karazikar is 3/3, and Rat tokens are 1/1. Choosing mode 2 means the spell has no valid targets and will be wasted.

Gem25F Timmy has Fleecemane Lion in hand (GW, 3/3) and has the mana to cast it (Forest + Wild Growth for GG, Sungrass Prairie + 1 for GW, Sol Ring for CC). They have 5+ mana available and could cast Fleecemane Lion and equip Sword of Hours to it (equip cost 2). Instead they passed without deploying any threats. Fleecemane Lion is an excellent creature that can later become hexproof/indestructible, and with Sword of Hours already on board, getting a creature out to equip it to is important. Even just casting the Lion alone would develop the board meaningfully.

Gem25F Timmy has Fleecemane Lion in hand (a 3/3 for GW) and has the mana to cast it (Forest + Wild Growth gives GG, Sungrass Prairie + 1 gives GW). With 5 lands, Sol Ring, and Wild Growth, there's plenty of mana available. Fleecemane Lion is a strong early creature that can later become hexproof and indestructible. Additionally, Sword of Hours is already on the battlefield waiting to be equipped. Deploying the Lion now would establish board presence and set up a future equip. Passing with unused mana and a castable creature is leaving value on the table.

Gem25F Timmy has untapped mana available (Island, Forest with Wild Growth, Forest, Sol Ring, Sungrass Prairie) and could cast Fleecemane Lion (GW) this turn. With 5+ mana available, they could cast the Lion and even equip Sword of Hours to it, developing their board. Instead they passed with significant unused mana, missing a land drop opportunity (no land played this turn based on board) and failing to deploy a threat. Fleecemane Lion is a strong 3/3 that can later become hexproof/indestructible, and getting it down earlier with equipment is valuable.

With 7 lands available, casting Solemn Simulacrum for 4 uses all mana and leaves nothing for interaction. Yavimaya Elder costs only 3 mana ({1}{G}{G}), leaving 4 mana open to cast Fact or Fiction at instant speed on an opponent's end step. This would yield both a creature on board AND a powerful card draw spell in the same turn cycle, rather than just one creature.

All opponents have no untapped creatures available to block. Solemn Simulacrum could attack for 2 free damage with zero risk. Even if it were somehow blocked and killed, it draws a card on death. Keeping it back as a blocker has some value with Karazikar on the board potentially goading creatures in future turns, but passing up guaranteed free damage seems suboptimal.

Playing Halimar Depths (enters tapped) instead of Swamp means only 4 mana available this turn instead of 5. With Swamp untapped, Haiku Villain could cast both Mind Stone (2) and Loyal Subordinate (2B) this turn, deploying two permanents and accelerating mana. With Halimar Depths tapped, they can only cast one. The scry-3 effect of Halimar Depths has value but can be played on a future turn when the tempo cost is lower.

Haiku Villain cast Loyal Subordinate (a 3/1 creature with menace and a Lieutenant ability that requires controlling your commander) before casting Mind Stone. Mind Stone provides mana acceleration that would help cast the expensive cards in hand (Sphinx of Uthuun at 7 mana, Adarkar Valkyrie at 6 mana, Lightform at 3 mana). The Loyal Subordinate's Lieutenant ability won't trigger since Aminatou isn't on the battlefield, making it just a vanilla 3/1 menace creature. Mind Stone would have been better as it accelerates toward the powerful 6+ mana cards in hand and can be sacrificed later to draw a card. Additionally, playing the Swamp from hand first (land drop) before casting either spell would have been correct sequencing, giving access to more mana options.

Playing Mountain instead of Swamp when the player already has 2 Mountains but only 1 Swamp. With Rakdos Charm (BR) in hand and Chittering Witch's ability (1B, sacrifice) available, having more black mana sources would be more valuable. The player already has more than enough red sources.

Attacking with all creatures including Prosper, Tome-Bound (commander and value engine with deathtouch) and Chittering Witch (utility creature with sacrifice ability) risks losing important non-combat pieces unnecessarily. Prosper generates card advantage each end step and Chittering Witch can sacrifice rats for removal.

Karazikar, the Eye Tyrant is a high-value multiplayer threat that goads creatures and draws cards whenever opponents attack each other. Leaving it on the board allows Sonnet Stoic to accumulate significant card advantage over multiple turns. Valorous Stance can cleanly destroy it (toughness 5 >= 4).

At the end of Sonnet Stoic's turn, Gem25F Timmy has untapped mana available (Island, Forest, Forest with Wild Growth, Sol Ring, Sungrass Prairie) and could activate Lumbering Falls to make it a 3/3 creature. While there's no immediate combat use for this, activating it at end of opponent's turn is generally low-cost and could be relevant if anything unexpected happens. However, the bigger consideration is whether Valorous Stance could be useful here - Karazikar, the Eye Tyrant (likely has toughness 4+) is a significant threat that forces attacks and gives the controller card advantage. Destroying it with Valorous Stance at instant speed at end of turn would be a clean answer to a dangerous threat, especially since it's already tapped.

Casting Fleecemane Lion before combat is slightly suboptimal. Timmy has Lumbering Falls that can animate into a 3/3 hexproof attacker, and holding the Lion until after combat would deny opponents information about board state. More importantly, casting Fertile Ground first would be better sequencing - it would enchant a land (like the Forest with Wild Growth, or another land) to generate extra mana, potentially allowing Timmy to both play Fleecemane Lion AND have mana available for Valorous Stance or to activate Lumbering Falls. Playing Fertile Ground on the untapped Forest would give access to more mana this turn.

Casting Minds Aglow in multiplayer gives all opponents free card draw. With 6 mana to pump into it, all 4 players draw those cards equally, giving opponents a combined 3x the cards Sarge draws. Sarge already has 6 cards in hand, so the marginal value is low, while opponents with fewer cards benefit more.

Passed the main phase with 6 mana available without deploying Yavimaya Elder, a strong value creature that would help ramp toward casting Damia next turn. Even if holding up Fact or Fiction for end-of-turn, they had enough mana to cast both Yavimaya Elder (1GG) and still have 3 mana remaining, though not quite enough for FoF (3U needs 4). They could at least advance their board with Elder.

Troll Ascetic (3/2 hexproof with regeneration available) was held back from attacking despite being one of the safest attackers in the format. With hexproof it can't be targeted by removal, and with regeneration mana available (has untapped Forests) it survives most blocks. Haiku Villain is at a vulnerable 13 life, making additional pressure valuable.

Gem3F Sarge declined to cast Fact or Fiction at the end of an opponent's combat step, which is the ideal time to cast it (end of combat or end of turn on an opponent's turn). They have 5 untapped lands (3 Swamps, 2 Forests, 1 Island) plus an untapped Solemn Simulacrum — wait, looking more carefully, the lands and creatures are tapped. Let me re-examine. The board shows Forest, Swamp, Swamp, Island, Forest with Troll Ascetic tapped and Swamp and Solemn Simulacrum tapped. That's 5 lands untapped and 1 Swamp tapped plus the two creatures tapped. Actually, none of the lands are marked as tapped — only Troll Ascetic and Solemn Simulacrum are tapped. So Sarge has 3 Swamps, 2 Forests, and 1 Island untapped = 6 mana available, more than enough to cast Fact or Fiction (3U). This is during Sarge's own combat step though, not an opponent's turn. Still, with 6 mana available and Fact or Fiction in hand, passing on casting it during their own combat (before second main) means they could cast it in their second main phase or save mana for something else. Since it's their own turn, they can cast it in main phase 2, so declining here is fine — sorcery-speed plays in main phase 2 are still available. Actually wait — Fact or Fiction is an instant, so casting it in combat is legal but there's no particular advantage over waiting for main phase 2. Declining is reasonable since they might want to sequence plays in main phase 2 after seeing the cards.

Gem3F Sarge declined to cast Fact or Fiction at the end of an opponent's combat step, which is the optimal time to cast it (end of opponent's turn or during combat). They have 4 untapped lands (3 Swamps, 1 Island, 2 Forests) plus a tapped Solemn Simulacrum, giving them access to at least 1 blue and 3 other mana - exactly enough to cast Fact or Fiction for {3}{U}. Casting it now would dig 5 cards deep and get cards into hand before their own turn, maximizing available mana on their turn for playing what they find. There's no reason to hold it since they have Spell Crumple for countermagic if needed, and the remaining untapped lands could still leave mana open. Actually, looking more carefully - the board shows Troll Ascetic and Solemn Simulacrum are tapped (likely from attacking), and looking at the lands: Forest, Swamp, Swamp, Island, Forest, Swamp - 6 lands total, but the tapped status isn't shown for all lands. Given that Fact or Fiction appears as a valid casting option, they must have sufficient untapped mana. Passing on an end-of-opponent's-turn Fact or Fiction is a missed opportunity for card advantage at the best possible timing.

Played Command Tower instead of Golgari Rot Farm when all lands were tapped. Since it's postcombat main and all lands are tapped, Golgari Rot Farm entering tapped has zero tempo cost. Playing the bounce land would net +1 mana going forward (bouncing a Swamp and replaying it next turn), which could enable casting Damia (7 mana) sooner while keeping up interaction.

Haiku Villain has a Swamp in hand but cast Mind Stone before playing their land for the turn. Playing the Swamp first would maximize available mana after casting Mind Stone, potentially enabling additional plays or leaving more mana open for future interactions.

annotation_description: Sacrificing Mind Stone for a card when holding two expensive spells (Sphinx of Uthuun at 7 mana, Adarkar Valkyrie at 6 mana) that require significant mana to cast. At 9 life, getting to 6-7 mana quickly is critical, and Mind Stone provides ongoing ramp. Lightform at 3 mana is the only castable spell and could be played next turn with current mana.

Haiku Villain is at 9 HP with no untapped blockers (Loyal Subordinate is tapped). Sonnet Stoic has Karazikar (5/5), Prosper (1/4), Chittering Witch (2/2), and 4 Rat Tokens (1/1 each) available. Only 2 creatures were sent to attack, likely dealing only 6-7 damage, failing to kill Haiku Villain. Sending Karazikar (5) + Chittering Witch (2) + 2 Rat Tokens (2) = 9 damage exactly lethal, or more for guaranteed kill.

The player has expensive cards like Acidic Slime (5 mana) and The Mimeoplasm (commander, 5 mana) that need more mana to cast. Playing a land costs nothing and increases future options.

Timmy has no untapped creatures to block, making a free 3 damage attack available. Even against Stoic, the Rat tokens are only 1/1s and Troll Ascetic would survive blocking. Passing up free damage, especially with a hexproof creature against a defenseless opponent, is suboptimal in a multiplayer game where chip damage matters.

Gem3F Sarge passed the turn with an unplayed land in hand (Barren Moor, Swamp, or Forest) while having only 6 lands on the battlefield. Missing a land drop delays casting powerful spells like Acidic Slime (5 mana) and The Mimeoplasm (5 mana commander). Even though Barren Moor enters tapped, playing it now costs nothing and provides an additional mana source next turn. With Acidic Slime in hand costing {3}{G}{G}, having 7 lands available next turn (or 6 untapped) is significantly better than 6.

Declined to play Barren Moor when it was a free land drop. With Acidic Slime (5 mana) and Spell Crumple (3 mana) in hand, every land matters. Playing Barren Moor tapped costs nothing and gets them closer to casting their more expensive spells.

The mana was available ({3}{G}{W}) and there was no pressing need to hold up mana for other plays.

Failed to play Barren Moor as their land drop for the turn. Playing it is pure upside - it enters tapped but provides an additional land for future turns. With Acidic Slime (5 mana) and Spell Crumple (3 mana) in hand, having more mana available is valuable. There's no reason to hold Barren Moor since playing it reduces hand size from 7 to 6 (no discard issues) while adding future mana.

annotation_description: Argentum Armor is unequipped and Gem25F Timmy has no creatures on the battlefield, making it a dormant threat. Meanwhile Sonnet Stoic at 40 life has the strongest active board with Karazikar and Prosper generating value, plus Sol Ring providing mana acceleration.

Passed priority without playing a land (Swamp or Barren Moor in hand) and without casting Stitch Together (BB) to return Yavimaya Elder from graveyard to hand. The reasoning about casting Acidic Slime was confused - Acidic Slime is not in hand, and the mentioned Argentum Armor target is already in Timmy's graveyard. Missing the land drop loses tempo and mana development.

Gem3F Sarge has an untapped Swamp and Barren Moor in hand with no meaningful instant-speed plays available. Cycling Barren Moor for {B} would draw a card at essentially no cost since the available untapped mana (Forest + Swamp) cannot be used for any relevant spell (Spell Crumple needs UU, Stitch Together is sorcery speed).

Failed to cycle Barren Moor with an untapped Swamp available and no other use for the mana. This is a free card draw opportunity that also advances graveyard count toward Stitch Together's threshold (currently at 5 cards in graveyard, threshold needs 7). The Barren Moor in hand is worse than a basic Swamp since it enters tapped, and Sarge already has a Swamp in hand for future land drops.

Hex requires 6 creature targets but there are very few opponent creatures, meaning Sonnet Stoic must destroy most of their own board (Karazikar, Prosper, Rat Token) just to kill opponents' creatures. Additionally, Troll Ascetic has hexproof and can't be targeted. Sonnet Stoic is trading away their key value engines (Karazikar, Prosper) to destroy essentially just Solemn Simulacrum (which draws Sarge a card on death).

Fiend of the Shadows was likely targeted by Hex and could have been saved by activating its regenerate ability (sacrifice a Human, no mana cost). Chittering Witch is a Human that was presumably also targeted by Hex, so sacrificing it to regenerate Fiend would save one creature at no additional cost since Chittering Witch was dying anyway.

message: Select an artifact or enchantment (to sacrifice)
annotation_description: Gem25F Timmy's reasoning shows fundamental confusion about being forced to sacrifice an artifact or enchantment to Tribute to the Wild. They stated they wanted to 'pass priority' when they are required to make a sacrifice choice. This confusion likely led to a suboptimal or random sacrifice selection. The correct sacrifice would be Sword of Hours (weakest card with no creature to equip and minimal impact), preserving Sol Ring and mana enchantments (Wild Growth/Fertile Ground) which are critical for their mana production.

Casting Prognostic Sphinx from exile (via Share the Spoils) is a decent threat but fuels Sonnet Stoic's Share the Spoils engine with another exile trigger. Meanwhile, Fleshbag Marauder for 3 mana would force Sonnet Stoic to sacrifice either Prosper, Tome-Bound (their key value engine) or Chittering Witch, which could be more impactful. Additionally, Desecrator Hag could retrieve Lhurgoyf from the graveyard, which would be very large given ~16 creature cards across all graveyards.

Only attacked with Vorosh when Troll Ascetic could likely also attack safely. With Timmy at 21 life and apparently no untapped blockers, sending both Vorosh and Troll Ascetic would deal 9 damage instead of 6. Troll Ascetic's hexproof makes it a safe attacker even without regeneration mana available.

Gem25F Timmy selected Skullbriar to attack but then skipped the attack entirely ('After: Gem25F Timmy skip attack'). With Skullbriar at 3/3 (with +1/+1 counters that persist) and Sword of Hours available, attacking is important for building Skullbriar's counter advantage. At 14 life facing two opponents, Timmy needs to be applying pressure. Additionally, Skullbriar gains a +1/+1 counter whenever it deals combat damage, plus Sword of Hours would add another counter and potentially double them. Missing this attack means losing significant counter-snowball potential.

Sonnet Stoic passed with 4 available mana (2 Mountains + Sol Ring) but couldn't cast any interaction anyway (no untapped black source for Terminate or Rakdos Charm). They should have deployed mana rocks from hand to develop their board. Fellwar Stone (2 mana) and Commander's Sphere (3 mana) could both have been cast, or at minimum one of them.

Fleshbag Marauder forces Sarge to sacrifice it (or Troll Ascetic), while Sonnet Stoic only loses a 1/1 Rat Token and Timmy has no creatures. This is a terrible exchange - spending a card and 3 mana to kill a token. The AI's reasoning hallucinated having Vorosh, Sphinx, and Mulldrifter on board when only Troll Ascetic was present.

Sonnet Stoic has 2 untapped Mountains and Fellwar Stone in hand (costs {2}), but chose to pass without casting it. Deploying the mana rock would provide additional mana acceleration for future turns, and there's no strategic reason to hold it.

Fleshbag Marauder is on the stack and will force each player to sacrifice a creature. Gem3F Sarge controls Troll Ascetic, which has regenerate available for {1}{G}. By activating regenerate on Troll Ascetic before Fleshbag Marauder resolves, the Troll would be set up with a regeneration shield, meaning when it's sacrificed... actually, regeneration doesn't prevent sacrifice. Sacrifice cannot be regenerated from. So declining to activate regenerate is correct since it wouldn't help against Fleshbag Marauder's sacrifice effect. However, the player could have activated Prognostic Sphinx's discard ability to give it hexproof (though hexproof also doesn't help against sacrifice). Neither ability helps here.
